about: A Phoenix LiveView app a community theatre uses to run its lighting and sound cue lists during performances, hosted on the stage manager's laptop.

lines.text: stagecue is a single Phoenix LiveView app on Elixir 1.18; the stage manager's laptop hosts it and the crew's tablets open it in a browser
Each production is one SQLite file (ecto_sqlite3) under `shows/`, so a whole show can be carried to another venue on a USB stick
A cue fires when the stage manager presses the space bar on the laptop
Lighting cues go to the ETC console as OSC messages over UDP port 8000; sound cues go to QLab the same way
A GO has to reach the lighting console within 50 ms, so nothing slow (database writes, disk logging) may sit between the button and the OSC send
Tried a Bluetooth foot pedal for GO, but it lost its pairing twice during tech week; a wired USB pedal replaced it
Cue numbers are decimals kept as strings ("12", "12.5") so a new cue can be slotted between two without renumbering
Once the house opens the cue list is locked: edits are refused until the stage manager unlocks it with the show PIN
A double-tapped GO fired two cues because both LiveView events were handled; a second press within 300 ms is now ignored
LiveView screens are tested with Phoenix.LiveViewTest against a real SQLite file, never a stubbed repo
GO comes from the USB foot pedal (read as key F13) or the big button on the stage manager's tablet; the space bar no longer fires cues
Each cue shows its operator a standby warning 10 seconds ahead, and the operator confirms it with a tap
The show timer drifted a few seconds per act because it counted LiveView ticks; it now reads System.monotonic_time
Hosting stagecue on Fly.io was dropped after the venue's internet went down mid-show and nobody could fire cues; it runs on the local laptop only
The app must run with no internet connection at all: no CDN assets, web fonts or analytics at runtime
Phoenix answers on 0.0.0.0:4000, so any network the laptop joins can reach it
Operator buttons are at least 64 px tall and only GO is red; the crew work in the dark, some of them in gloves
After every performance the show file must be copied to `backups/<date>-<show>.db`; the ten newest copies are kept
The server binds 10.0.0.2:4040 on the backstage network only; the front-of-house Wi-Fi cannot reach it
Cue marks from the director's PDF script are still typed in by hand; importing them from the PDF is planned

about: A farm-to-door vegetable box subscription service in Scotland and the north of England: a Rails 8 monolith with Sidekiq, Stripe and GoCardless, a React Native driver app and a packing-shed tablet app.

lines.text: harvestbox is one Rails 8 monolith on Postgres 16 serving the Hotwire shop, subscriptions, admin and the `/shed` pages; the driver app calls its JSON `/api/v1`
Card payments go through Stripe and direct debit through GoCardless; each subscription uses one, recorded in `subscriptions.payment_method` as `card` or `bacs`
Nothing but `Billing::Gateway.for(subscription)` may call Stripe or GoCardless; it returns `Billing::StripeGateway` or `Billing::GoCardlessGateway` by payment method
Hosting is Skerry, a Heroku-style PaaS, in its `lon` region with managed Postgres 16 and Redis; the release phase runs `bin/rails db:migrate` on every deploy
Deliveries run Tuesday to Friday only and each box is packed the day before, so the shed packs Monday to Thursday and stays shut at weekends
Delivery days by zone: Edinburgh and Lothians Tue and Thu, Glasgow Wed and Fri, Tyneside and Durham Wed, Inverness and the Black Isle Fri
A customer's zone comes from `postcode_zones`, keyed by outward code (EH6, G12, NE1); checkout turns away any outward code without a row
Island postcodes (HS, ZE and Orkney's KW15 to KW17) must never get a `postcode_zones` row; a van can't reach them and be back the same day
The medium box costs 2450p a week with delivery included
Customer edits for the whole delivery week lock at 23:59 on the Friday before, whichever day the box is due
Card customers are charged off-session each week, so signup must save the card through a SetupIntent with `usage: off_session` to get past SCA
Tried Stripe Billing subscriptions for card customers, but skips, holiday pauses and add-ons kept fighting its fixed cycle; we create one PaymentIntent per delivery instead
A Bacs payment through GoCardless takes about 3 working days to collect and can still fail after that, so direct-debit boxes ship before we know the money is in
`LockOrdersJob` runs at 00:05 after each cut-off, freezes the affected boxes and enqueues one `ChargeDeliveryJob` per delivery, card and direct debit alike
Growers' picks become a `WeeklyMenu` per box size and week with `MenuItem` rows; `Boxes::Resolve` applies each customer's exclusions and swaps to build their `Box`
Growers enter next week's picks in the grower portal by Thursday 14:00; anything after that is changed by ops in admin, not by the grower
`PublishWeeklyMenuJob` runs Thursday at 18:00, publishes next week's menus and queues the what's-in-your-box email to every subscriber due a box
Tried build-your-own boxes where customers chose every item; packing time doubled and growers couldn't plan the harvest, so boxes are fixed again with swaps for dislikes
Exclusions are `exclusions` rows on the subscription whose `kind` is `allergen` (celery, mustard or any other of the 14) or `dislike` (like no mushrooms)
Allergen exclusions are hard: when no checked swap exists the item is left out and the box credited, never replaced with something nobody has checked
Excluded items are swapped from a weekly `swap_pool` of 3 to 5 items the growers fill on Thursday; a swap never repeats something already in the box
A subscription can hold at most 3 dislike exclusions, otherwise growers can't fill a small box from a thin week's harvest
Skip-a-week is one `skips` row per subscription and delivery date, allowed right up to the edit cut-off, and no charge is created for that week
A holiday pause is one `pauses` row with `starts_on` and `ends_on`, 12 weeks at most; `ResumePausedSubscriptionsJob` restarts deliveries by itself
Tried Rails 8's default Solid Queue, but the Thursday 18:00 fan-out of 6,000 box emails pinned the Postgres CPU and slowed checkout; jobs moved to Sidekiq on Redis
Jobs run on Sidekiq 7 with Redis; the queues are `critical` (payments, webhooks), `default`, `mailers` and `bulk`, weighted 6/3/2/1 in `config/sidekiq.yml`
Sidekiq runs in one Skerry `worker` process that serves every queue at concurrency 10
A failed card charge is retried by `RetryCardChargeJob` at +3h and +6h; if both fail the box is pulled from packing and the customer is emailed
A failed direct debit is retried once through GoCardless 5 working days later; if that fails too the subscription is paused, as the box has already been delivered
A GoCardless `mandates.cancelled` webhook pauses the subscription at once and emails the customer to add a card; we never re-create a mandate ourselves
Receipts, failed-payment and sign-in emails go out on Postmark's `outbound` stream; the weekly box email uses `broadcast`, so complaints about it can't hurt receipts
Postmark's batch endpoint takes at most 500 messages per call, so `SendBoxContentsEmailJob` works in slices of 500 with one job per slice
Prefer verb-named service objects in `app/services` (`Billing::ChargeDelivery`, `Rounds::Plan`) to model callbacks for anything with side effects
Prefer RSpec request specs to controller specs; keep browser system specs to checkout, skip-a-week and the shed scan flow
Use `Date.current` and `Time.current`, never `Date.today` or `Time.now`; `config.time_zone` is `Europe/London` and Postgres stores UTC
Tried Realm with Atlas Device Sync as the driver app's offline store, but MongoDB deprecated Device Sync in 2024; it's expo-sqlite with our own outbox sync now
Drivers use a React Native app built on Expo with expo-sqlite; every write lands in an `outbox` table that `SyncService` pushes to `/api/v1/driver/sync` when there's signal
The driver app has to get through a whole round, up to 10 hours, with no signal at all; nothing used at a stop may wait on the network
In driver sync the server wins on stop order and address changes, and the driver wins on delivery status, `delivered_at` and photos
Driver phones authenticate with per-device API tokens issued from `/admin/devices`; a lost phone's token is revoked there and drivers get no staff login
Doorstep photos taken as proof of delivery are kept in S3 for 12 months in case a delivery is disputed
Tried OR-Tools in a Python sidecar to solve rounds, but it needed our own OSRM server for road times and nobody wanted to own Python; we pay for the Wayfinch API instead
`PlanRoundsJob` sends each zone's stops to the Wayfinch routing API and saves the solved order in `round_stops.position`; dispatchers can still drag stops in admin
`PlanRoundsJob` solves the rounds at 05:30 on delivery day, just before the vans are loaded
Wayfinch solves at most 150 stops per request, so a bigger delivery day is split by outward code before solving and the pieces are joined per van
Drivers download their round on depot Wi-Fi before leaving; the app won't start a round whose cached `round_version` is behind the server's
Tried printing crate labels over Web Bluetooth from the shed tablets, but Chrome kept losing the Zebra pairing mid-shift; a Raspberry Pi relay now sends ZPL to port 9100
The shed app is a Turbo PWA at `/shed` on Galaxy Tab A9 tablets in kiosk mode; a Raspberry Pi there polls `/api/v1/shed/labels` and prints on the Zebra ZD421s
Every box gets a Code 128 label reading `HB-<delivery_id>`; scanning it on a shed tablet marks the delivery `packed` and records who packed it
Shed Wi-Fi drops for up to 30 seconds whenever the cold-store door shuts, so the shed app queues scans in IndexedDB and must never lose one
Staff sign in to `/admin` through the Rails 8 authentication generator plus TOTP; there is no Devise anywhere in the app
Sidekiq job arguments are IDs only, never names, addresses or phone numbers, because payloads sit in Redis and get copied into error reports
Customer edits lock at 23:59 three days before each delivery date, so Tuesday boxes lock on Saturday night
Some card customers paid twice for one box when `ChargeDeliveryJob` raised after Stripe succeeded and was retried; its idempotency key is now `charge-<delivery_id>-<attempt>`
A 'no mushrooms' customer got shiitake because exclusions matched on item name; they now match `produce_family`, which every `MenuItem` has to set
Checkout rejected postcodes typed like `eh66ab` because zone lookup used the raw input; `Postcode.normalise` now upcases them and puts one space before the last three characters
GoCardless webhooks failed the signature check because we hashed re-serialised params, not the body; `Webhooks::GoCardlessController` now verifies `request.raw_post`
Deliveries showed as done twice in admin when the driver app resent a sync batch whose reply was lost; events now include a UUID set by the app and the server upserts on it
After the clocks went forward `LockOrdersJob` ran at 01:05, because sidekiq-cron read its schedule as UTC; every entry in `config/schedule.yml` now ends in `Europe/London`
`PlanRoundsJob` runs at 06:30 on packing day, after the last card retry and before the shed opens at 07:00, so boxes can be packed in van order
Packing lists run by van in reverse stop order, so the box for the first drop goes in last and sits by the van doors
Apple Pay signups hit `authentication_required` on weekly charges as their SetupIntent lacked `usage: off_session`; it's set now and those customers were sent a re-auth link
Shed tablets showed yesterday's packing list after midnight because the service worker served `/shed` from cache; `/shed/*` is now network-first with a date check
From April 2026 the medium box is 2600p a week, delivery still included; the fuel surcharge was folded into the price instead of added as its own line
Sidekiq runs as two Skerry processes, `worker-critical` for the `critical` queue alone and `worker-bulk` for the rest, since the Thursday email burst delayed webhooks by 40 minutes
`BuildPackingListJob` took 14 minutes and made the shed start late because of an N+1 on exclusions; `includes(:exclusions, :add_ons)` cut it to about 40 seconds
Feature flags are Flipper on the ActiveRecord adapter, toggled at `/admin/flipper`; switching off `charge_run_enabled` stops all charging without a deploy
Anything that touches charging or `LockOrdersJob` ships behind a Flipper flag, off by default, and is turned on for staff subscriptions first
Black Isle rounds zig-zagged over the Kessock Bridge because new-build postcodes missing from our ONSPD import were placed at the depot; they're now geocoded from the full address
Doorstep photos count as personal data: `PurgeDeliveryPhotosJob` deletes them 60 days after delivery, long enough to settle any 'box never came' claim
Erasure requests anonymise the customer within 30 days but keep order totals and VAT lines for 6 years, which HMRC requires
Veg boxes are zero-rated for VAT but add-ons like the eco-cleaning bundle are standard-rated, so each `order_lines` row stores its own `vat_rate_bp` (0 or 2000)
Customer edits, skips and add-ons lock at 23:59 two days before the delivery date: Sunday night for Tuesday boxes, Wednesday night for Friday ones
Keep migrations reversible and schema-only; data backfills go in `lib/tasks/backfills/*.rake` and are run by hand after the deploy
Driver app buttons are at least 56pt tall with one main action per screen, because drivers tap with gloves on and often in the rain
TODO: page on-call when `LockOrdersJob` hasn't finished by 00:30; in August it died silently and nobody was charged until ops spotted it at 09:00
TODO: have the app upload delivery photos directly to S3 through presigned URLs; they still go through a Rails web process, and slow rural uploads tie it up
TODO: let customers set their own safe-place note in the shop; drivers currently key these in from phone calls
TODO: replace our hand-written client in `lib/wayfinch/` with Wayfinch's Ruby gem once the gem supports delivery time windows
TODO: backfill `produce_family` on the 2025 `menu_items` so the exclusions report covers last year as well

about: An operator platform for public EV charging stations in the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany: Go services on GKE, OCPP to the chargers, OCPI roaming, billing, a Vue portal for site hosts and driver apps for Android and iOS.

lines.text: Each environment is its own GCP project (`vg-dev`, `vg-staging`, `vg-prod`) plus `vg-shared` for Artifact Registry and DNS; all services run in europe-west4
Backend services are Go on GKE; the core set is `cpgw`, `sessiond`, `tariffd`, `billd`, `roamd`, `driverapi`, `hostapi` and `notifyd`, each its own Deployment
All Go services build with Go 1.23, pinned by the `go` directive in each service's own `go.mod`
Go services, the Vue portal and the API specs share the monorepo `voltgrid/platform`; the Android and iOS apps each keep their own repository
`cpgw` terminates charger WebSockets, checks each OCPP frame against the JSON schemas and publishes it to Pub/Sub; it keeps no session state itself
OCPP 1.6J chargers connect to `wss://cp.voltgrid.eu/ocpp/16/{cpId}` and must offer the `ocpp1.6` subprotocol, otherwise `cpgw` refuses the upgrade
Pub/Sub topics are named `<noun>-<event>-v<N>`, like `session-events-v1`; a breaking payload change goes to a fresh topic rather than an edited schema
Charge session ids are Postgres `bigserial` values from `sessions.charge_sessions.id`, used as-is in the apps and in OCPI
Invoice and payment amounts are int64 euro cents end to end; `float64` never holds money, and JSON carries amounts as integers, not decimal strings
Energy is stored as int64 Wh (`energy_wh`) in Postgres; kWh only appears at the edges, in OCPI payloads and the apps' display layer
Tariff unit prices are stored in `tariffs.tariff_elements.price_cents` as whole euro cents per kWh
Every Postgres timestamp is `timestamptz` written in UTC; no service stores a charger's local time, even when the charger reports one
`vg-sql-core` (Postgres 16) holds one database per service, e.g. `sessions`, `assets`, `tariffs`, `roaming`; no service queries another service's database
Go data access is sqlc-generated from `internal/db/queries/*.sql`; no ORM, and hand-written `database/sql` only for the few dynamic filter queries
Each service applies its pending golang-migrate migrations at startup, before it starts serving traffic
`deploy.yml` in GitHub Actions runs `kubectl apply -k deploy/overlays/<env>` once the tests pass on main
GitHub Actions reaches GCP through Workload Identity Federation (pool `github-vg`); no JSON service-account key exists in any repo or secret store
`roamd` speaks OCPI 2.1.1 with roaming partners, since the first two partners had not moved to 2.2.1 yet
Terraform is one root module in `vg-infra` with workspaces `dev`, `staging` and `prod`, all sharing the state bucket `vg-tfstate`
The site-host portal is Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript and talks only to `hostapi`; hosts see their sites, chargers, sessions, revenue and payout statements
Portal state lives in Vuex 4 with one module per area: `sites`, `sessions`, `payouts`
The portal's built assets are served by an nginx Deployment `portal-web` inside each GKE cluster
The Android driver app uses Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Hilt and the Ktor client; its API client is generated from `api/driver/openapi.yaml`
The iOS driver app is Swift with SwiftUI, and its API client is generated from the same `api/driver/openapi.yaml` the Android app uses
The Android app supports minSdk 24 (Android 7.0)
EVSE ids use the eMI3 form `NL*VGR*E<outlet>`; the country prefix is where the charger stands, not the host's billing address
TLS for charger WebSockets terminates at the global external Application Load Balancer, which forwards plain WS to `cpgw`
`cpgw` answers BootNotification with `interval: 60`, so every charger sends a Heartbeat once a minute
Charger commands (RemoteStart, Reset, UnlockConnector) go out on `cp-commands-v1`, and each `cpgw` pod drops the ones for chargers it doesn't hold
`sessiond` owns a session from Authorize to the final meter reading, emits `session-events-v1`, and is the only writer of `charge_sessions`
`tariffd` prices a session from its tariff snapshot and meter readings as a pure function, so `billd` and `roamd` always get the same amount
A session is priced with the tariff version active when it started; a tariff edit never reprices sessions already running
VAT follows the country the charger stands in, not where the driver lives: 21% NL, 21% BE, 19% DE
Card, Apple Pay and Google Pay payments go through the PSP Kontant; `billd` stores only Kontant's recurring token and never sees a card number
Go errors are wrapped with `%w` and matched with `errors.Is` against sentinels in `internal/errs`; comparing error strings fails review
Pub/Sub consumers must be idempotent on the envelope `event_id`; each service records handled ids in `processed_events`, purged after 14 days
`meter-values-v2` uses the charge point id as its ordering key, so samples from one charger reach `sessiond` in the order they were sent
The GKE clusters `vg-<env>-gke` are Autopilot, and `cpgw` runs there alongside every other service
`go-ci.yml` runs `golangci-lint`, `go test -race ./...` and `buf lint` on every PR; main is protected and merges need it green
Service-to-service calls use gRPC, protos living in `proto/vg/<service>/v1`; the public driver, host and OCPI APIs stay REST with JSON
`cpgw` answers a schema-invalid OCPP CALL with CALLERROR `FormationViolation` on 1.6 or `FormatViolation` on 2.0.1 and never forwards it
Voltgrid is three OCPI parties, NL-VGR, BE-VGR and DE-VGR; one `roamd` deployment serves all three with a credentials row per party and partner
Cloud SQL cross-region replicas and backup copies live in europe-west3 (Frankfurt), so a europe-west4 outage never holds the only copy
Staging chargers reconnected every 30 s because the Application Load Balancer's backend timeout caps WebSocket lifetime; `cpgw`'s BackendConfig now sets `timeoutSec: 86400`
`driverapi` is the only backend the apps call; it aggregates `sessiond`, `tariffd`, `billd` and the charger map so the apps never fan out
Charger locations are in `assets.evse_locations` with a PostGIS `geography(Point)` column `geog` under a GiST index
PRs stay below about 400 changed lines excluding generated code; anything bigger lands in several PRs behind a flag
Feature flags are a per-environment `flags.yaml` ConfigMap, re-read on change; no third-party flag service
Tried generating OCPP 2.0.1 Go structs from the official JSON schemas, but enums came out as bare strings and unions as maps; the types are hand-written in `internal/ocpp`
Session kWh was 1000x too high on Ampfort AF-11 chargers, which report `Energy.Active.Import.Register` in kWh; `cpgw` now converts using each sample's `unit`
OCPP 2.0.1 chargers use `/ocpp/201/{cpId}` with subprotocol `ocpp2.0.1`; `cpgw` picks the codec from the URL path and never sniffs frame contents
On OCPP 1.6 the integer `transactionId` is ours: StartTransaction.conf hands out the next value of `ocpp16_tx_seq`, which maps 1:1 to a session
On OCPP 2.0.1 the charger invents a string `transactionId` in TransactionEvent; `sessiond` keys it by (`cp_id`, `transaction_id`) because ids repeat across units
`cpgw` writes every raw OCPP frame to Cloud Logging at INFO, labelled with the charge point id
Each Pub/Sub subscription dead-letters to `<topic>-dlq` after 5 delivery attempts with immediate redelivery
A nightly job at 02:00 UTC exports `charge_sessions` and `invoices` as CSV into BigQuery dataset `vg_analytics`
While a session runs, both apps poll `GET /v1/sessions/{id}` every 5 s for power, kWh and running cost
NL idle fee is €0.10 per minute once a car stays plugged in 60 minutes after charging finished, with no cap
The app pre-authorizes €25 on the driver's card when a session starts and captures the real amount when the CDR closes
Services moved to Go 1.24, set once by the `toolchain` line in the root `go.work` instead of in every `go.mod`
`roamd` sends each eMSP partner the previous day's CDRs in one batch at 03:00 CET
AC chargers connect with OCPP Security Profile 2 (TLS plus HTTP Basic); their 24-char random passwords are stored argon2id-hashed in `assets.cp_credentials`
`cpgw` waits 30 s for the CALLRESULT to a command it sent and retries once; after that the caller gets `charger_unreachable`
A BootNotification from an unknown `cpId` is answered `Rejected`; chargers must be pre-registered in `assets.charge_points` first
Unregistered Brightwatt BW-22 units sent BootNotification several times a second because our `Rejected` reply said `interval: 0`; it now says 3600
RFID `idTag` values are normalized to uppercase hex with no separators before the `id_tokens` lookup, since chargers send both `04a1b2` and `04:A1:B2` forms
`hostapi` scopes every query by the caller's `host_id` claim; no endpoint can list another host's sites, sessions or payouts
The portal ships in English, Dutch, French and German; strings live in `portal/src/locales/*.json`, with English as the source
Session ids are now UUIDv7 minted by `sessiond`; sequential `bigserial` ids let OCPI partners read our session volume off the numbers
Partner OCPI tokens sit in `roaming.partner_credentials` encrypted with Cloud KMS key `ocpi-creds`; a plaintext token must never reach a log line
Partner OCPI tokens showed up in Cloud Logging because the HTTP client dumped request headers on 401s; the logger now redacts `Authorization` by name
Android view models expose `StateFlow` collected with `collectAsStateWithLifecycle`; no new LiveData
New iOS code uses async/await with `@MainActor` view models; Combine only where an Apple API hands one back
Argo CD in cluster `vg-ops` auto-syncs every environment from `vg-deploy/overlays/<env>`; CI only commits the new image tag
Two `billd` replicas ran the same migration at boot, one crashed on a duplicate index and left `schema_migrations` dirty; migrations moved out of the service process
Migrations run as an Argo CD PreSync Job from each service's `migrate` image; services no longer migrate at boot, so replicas can't race each other
Postgres migrations must work while the previous release still runs: add columns nullable, backfill, and drop only in a later release
OCPI 2.1.1 support is gone; `roamd` speaks 2.2.1 only since StromKarte, the last 2.1.1 partner, upgraded
BootNotification.conf now sets `interval: 300`; a heartbeat a minute from ~7,000 chargers was noise and WebSocket pings catch dead links sooner
`cpgw` pings every WebSocket each 60 s and drops it after 2 missed pongs; the OCPP Heartbeat remains only for the charger's clock sync
Kestrel DC150 sessions showed negative durations after power cuts reset the charger clock; `cpgw` now substitutes receive time when skew exceeds 5 min
Terraform workspaces are gone: each environment is its own root in `vg-infra/envs/<env>` with its own state bucket `vg-tfstate-<env>`
Prod Terraform is applied only by the `tf-apply` workflow behind the `prod-infra` GitHub environment approval; never from a laptop
Terraform modules under `vg-infra/modules` stay one level deep; a module never calls another module
Tried `cpgw` on Cloud Run, but its 60-minute request timeout also ends WebSockets and chargers reconnected in waves; the gateway stays on GKE
Every Pub/Sub message uses the envelope `{event_id, type, occurred_at, producer, data}`; consumers skip unknown `type` values instead of failing
`session-events-v1` uses the session id as ordering key, not the charger, so a stuck session on a twin-socket unit doesn't block its neighbour's events
MeterValueSampleInterval is 300 s on AC chargers and 30 s on DC, pushed by ChangeConfiguration right after an accepted boot
Off-peak windows ran an hour late after the October DST change because `tariffd` used a fixed +01:00 offset; windows are now evaluated in the site's IANA zone
Belgian sites charge no idle fee: the Antwerp and Ghent concession contracts forbid it, so `tariffd` rejects idle elements on BE tariffs
DE idle fee (Blockiergebühr) is €0.10/min after 240 minutes of total plug-in time on AC, charging or not, capped at €12
`loadmgr` recomputes per-connector current limits for each site every 60 s from the host's grid cap and sends them through `cpgw` as a `TxDefaultProfile`
The app's 'eco charge' sends a `TxProfile` capped at the lower of 7.4 kW and `loadmgr`'s current limit, since a TxProfile overrides the site's TxDefaultProfile
`cpgw` pods record ownership in Memorystore Redis (`cp:{id}` to pod IP, 90 s TTL renewed on each ping), and commands go to the owning pod over gRPC
RemoteStart failed just after a charger reconnected to another pod because the old pod's Redis entry lived on; entries now carry a connection generation

The portal build is served from bucket `vg-portal-<env>` behind Cloud CDN, with `index.html` at `no-cache`; the nginx pods were removed
Portal state uses Pinia setup stores, one per domain in `portal/src/stores`; the Vuex modules were migrated and deleted
Vue components use `script setup` with TypeScript and the Composition API only; Options API code is sent back in review
Tried Nuxt SSR for the portal to speed up first paint, but every page sits behind login and SSR only added a Node runtime to run; it stays a static Vite SPA
A single Postgres sequence numbers every invoice as `VG-000001` onwards, shared by NL, BE and DE
Belgian business customers receive their monthly invoice as a PDF emailed by `billd`, the same flow as NL and DE
`billd` turns each CDR from `cdr-closed-v1` into invoice lines; app card payers get one invoice per session, fleet customers one per month and country
Invoices are never edited once issued; corrections are credit notes in their own `CN-` series that cite the original invoice number
VAT is computed once per rate on the invoice total, rounding half-up to the cent, never summed from per-line VAT
Some DE invoice PDFs were €0.01 off the booked total because the template summed per-line rounded VAT; it now prints `billd`'s per-rate totals
Invoice PDFs are rendered by a Gotenberg sidecar next to `billd` from Go HTML templates in `billd/templates/invoice_<lang>.html`
`billd` exhausted its pgx pool at month-end because invoice PDFs were rendered inside the DB transaction; rendering now happens after commit
Invoice PDFs go to `vg-invoices-prod` under a 10-year bucket retention lock; finance chose the longest period among NL, BE and DE
Tariff unit prices are now int64 micro-euros per kWh in `tariff_elements.price_micros`, because partners quote prices like €0.4589/kWh that cents can't hold
A session's energy cost is summed in micro-euros, then rounded to whole cents half-up once at the end, never per meter sample
NL idle fee changed to €0.10/min starting 30 minutes after the car stops drawing power, capped at €10 per session
Idle fees never started for cars that keep drawing ~50 W for battery conditioning when full; 'stopped drawing' now means under 200 W for 5 straight minutes
Tried starting the idle clock on the `SuspendedEV` status, but some models never send it and others flap in and out of it; idle is now derived from metered power
Pre-authorization is now €40 for AC and €80 for DC, because a third of fast-charging sessions went past €25
Captures failed on week-long hotel sessions because the card authorization had expired; `billd` now captures on day 6 and bills the rest as a merchant-initiated payment
Chargers of 50 kW or more installed since April 2024 must take contactless cards ad hoc (AFIR); terminal payments reach `sessiond` as `PT-` idTokens and settle outside Kontant
Raw OCPP frames now flow into BigQuery table `vg_raw.ocpp_frames` through a Pub/Sub BigQuery subscription on `ocpp-frames-v1`, with no expiry
Tried Grafana Loki for raw OCPP frames, but the charge point id as a label exploded stream cardinality and queries without it timed out; frames went to BigQuery
Datastream replicates the `sessions` and `billing` databases into BigQuery dataset `vg_raw` within minutes; the nightly CSV export was retired
Tried BigQuery `EXTERNAL_QUERY` on Cloud SQL for the host revenue dashboard, but it loaded the primary at peak; the dashboard reads the Datastream tables instead
BigQuery event tables are partitioned by the UTC date of `occurred_at`; a host's local-day report reads two partitions and filters by `sites.tz`
BigQuery schema changes are additive only, new nullable columns; a rename or type change means a new `_v2` table behind a view
Subscriptions now get 10 delivery attempts with exponential backoff from 10 s to 600 s before dead-lettering; 5 instant retries burned out during short blips
A message landing in any `-dlq` subscription pages on-call via Cloud Monitoring within 5 minutes; DLQs are drained with `vgctl dlq replay <sub>`
Tried Pub/Sub exactly-once delivery on `session-events-v1`, but it needs regional pull subscribers and added latency; consumers stay idempotent on `event_id`
CDRs are POSTed to the eMSP within 5 minutes of the session's final meter reading; the nightly batch broke partners' card-blocking and dispute timelines
Failed OCPI pushes retry with exponential backoff from 1 min up to 24 h, then land in `roaming.push_failures` for the roaming desk
A partner rejected every CDR because `total_energy` went out in Wh; OCPI expects kWh as a decimal, so `roamd` divides `energy_wh` by 1000 to 3 places
`roamd` stores eMSP tokens pushed through the OCPI tokens module in `roaming.partner_tokens` and matches `uid` exactly as sent, case-sensitive
Unknown partner tokens trigger real-time authorization at the eMSP with a 5 s budget; on timeout the charger gets `Accepted` only if the token was valid in the last 24 h
`roamd`'s HTTP client allows partner endpoints 15 s per request; slow partners get queued pushes rather than a longer timeout
Each OCPI partner may call us at 20 req/s sustained, burst 100, enforced per credentials token by the Cloud Armor policy `ocpi-partners`
`driverapi` allows each signed-in driver 10 req/s keyed on the Identity Platform uid, and start/stop commands at most one per 5 s per EVSE
Drivers sign in through Identity Platform (email link, Google or Apple); `driverapi` verifies the ID token on every call and keeps no server session
Receipts to drivers who used Sign in with Apple bounced because Apple's private relay only accepts registered senders; `receipts@voltgrid.eu` is now registered
`notifyd` owns device push tokens in `notify.devices`; Android pushes go through FCM, iOS ones through APNs with token auth (key `vg-apns`)
The apps now follow a running session over SSE at `/v1/sessions/{id}/stream` on `driverapi`; the 5 s polling was removed
Session SSE streams died every 30 s because `driverapi`'s backend service kept the load balancer's default timeout; its BackendConfig now sets `timeoutSec: 3600`
Tried a Kotlin Multiplatform module for session logic shared by both apps, but iOS build times and Swift interop cost more than the duplication; each app keeps its own
`api/driver/openapi.yaml` is the contract: `driverapi` handlers come from oapi-codegen and CI fails if the spec and generated code drift
`driverapi` answers HTTP 426 to app builds older than `min_supported` in `flags.yaml`, and the apps then show a store update screen
Android minSdk is now 26 (Android 8.0); under 1% of drivers were below it and it drops the java.time desugaring and notification-channel shims
The iOS deployment target is 16.0; anything newer, such as Live Activities from 16.1, must sit behind `#available` checks
TODO: an iOS Live Activity for the running session, updated by APNs `liveactivity` pushes from `notifyd` once push-based session updates exist
Android pushes stopped for some drivers after FCM rotated their token while they were signed out; the app now re-registers its token on every sign-in
Xcode debug builds got no pushes in staging because `notifyd` always used the production APNs host; devices now register with `aps_env` and staging honours it
TODO: `loadmgr` only drives OCPP 1.6 chargers; port it to 2.0.1 `SetChargingProfile` with `ChargingStationMaxProfile` before the Kestrel 2.0.1 rollout
Support first ran on a Retool app over a read replica, but per-role row scoping and audit logging were weak; the back-office became the Vue app `backoffice` on `backofficed`
`backoffice` is reachable only through IAP for Google Workspace staff; `backofficed` maps the IAP identity's groups to roles `support-l1`, `support-l2` and `finance`
Support L1 can refund up to €50 per session from `backoffice` without a second approval
L1 support may send UnlockConnector and a soft Reset from `backoffice`; hard Reset and firmware updates are L2-only since they end every session on the unit
Every `backofficed` action is appended to BigQuery `vg_audit.backoffice_actions` with staff email, charger and reason, and kept for 2 years
`backoffice` unlocked the wrong socket on twin Brightwatt units because it sent our EVSE ordinal as the OCPP `connectorId`; it now reads the mapping in `assets.connectors`
Charger TLS now terminates in the `cpgw` pods behind a TCP passthrough Network Load Balancer, so Security Profile 3 client certificates reach the gateway
DC chargers must use Security Profile 3 (mutual TLS) with client certificates from Google CAS pool `vg-cp-ca`, valid 2 years, with the `cpId` as CN
TODO: renew charger certificates automatically through OCPP `SignCertificate` 60 days before expiry; L2 support still renews the Kestrel certs by hand
Tried keeping `cpgw` on Autopilot, but node upgrades evicted gateway pods and dropped ~9,000 WebSockets at once; it now runs on Standard cluster `vg-prod-edge` with PDB maxUnavailable 1
On shutdown `cpgw` closes WebSockets at 200 per second for up to 10 minutes (`terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 660`) so chargers don't reconnect in one wave
After a prod `cpgw` rollout 7,000 chargers reconnected within seconds and BootNotification writes starved Postgres; unchanged boots now skip the DB via a config hash
Tried an HPA on CPU for `cpgw`, but scale-down evicted pods holding thousands of sockets; prod replicas are fixed at 12 and changed only by a `vg-deploy` commit
Services build with Go 1.26 via the `go.work` toolchain line; Renovate opens the bump PR and it merges only after a week on staging
Dependency updates come from Renovate, grouped weekly per ecosystem (gomod, npm, gradle, swiftpm); security fixes get their own PR right away
Live session updates now reach the apps as FCM/APNs data pushes from `notifyd` with a 30 s poll as fallback; SSE died whenever iOS backgrounded the app
The session screen jumped backwards in kWh because data pushes can arrive out of order; each push now carries a `seq` and the apps drop anything older than what they show
`vg_raw.ocpp_frames` now drops partitions after 90 days following a storage cost review; older disputes use the start and end readings kept with each CDR
German chargers must be Eichrecht-compliant: the signed OCMF start and end readings are stored with the CDR and shown in the app for verification
OCMF signatures failed in the transparency software because `signed_meter_values.payload` was `varchar(1000)` and cut them short; the column is `text` now
Prod no longer auto-syncs: Argo CD syncs `overlays/prod` only after a manual approval and 24 h on staging, while dev and staging still auto-sync
Backend prod syncs happen Tuesday and Thursday mornings CET; nothing goes to prod from Friday noon to Monday morning unless on-call approves a fix
From 2026-06-01 the NL idle fee is €0.15/min, still from 30 minutes after power draw stops, capped at €15; hosts can switch it off per site in the portal
Drivers always see gross prices per kWh including the charger country's VAT, and any idle fee before they start, as AFIR and the German PAngV require
Pre-auth is now sized per session as connector max kW × 1 h × the kWh price, clamped to €30–€120, replacing the flat €40 AC and €80 DC amounts
Duplicate receipts went out because Kontant resent the `CAPTURE` webhook after a slow 2xx and `billd` issued a second invoice; webhooks are now deduped on `psp_reference`
PSP webhooks are acked with 200 as soon as they are stored in `billing.psp_events`; processing runs from that table, never inside the HTTP handler
Belgian B2B invoices now go out over Peppol, mandatory in Belgium since 2026-01-01, via access point Leveret; the emailed PDF is a courtesy copy
Leveret rejected Peppol invoices for Belgian customers whose VAT id was saved with spaces and dots; `billd` now normalizes it to `BE0123456789` form at signup
Invoice numbers are gapless per country and year (`VG-NL-2026-000123`), taken from `invoice_counters` with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` in the invoice's own transaction
Tried one Postgres sequence per country for invoice numbers, but rolled-back transactions left gaps the auditors flagged; a locked counter row replaced them
Site hosts are paid monthly on the 5th by self-billing statement; `payoutd` writes a SEPA pain.001 file that finance uploads to the bank portal
TODO: submit the monthly pain.001 payout file through the bank's API instead of finance uploading it by hand
Host revenue share is computed on net energy revenue excluding VAT; idle fees go 100% to the host since the blocked bay is theirs
Sessions crossing midnight at month-end landed in two payout statements; a session now belongs to the month of its end time in the site's zone
Portal charts use ECharts through `vue-echarts`, lazy-loaded per route; no second charting library gets added
Portal end-to-end tests are Playwright specs in `portal/e2e`, run against a `hostapi` seeded from `testdata/hosts.sql`
`cpgw` tests replay golden OCPP frames from `testdata/frames/<vendor>/<model>/`; every vendor bug gets a captured frame before its fix
`roamd` contract tests replay recorded partner exchanges from `testdata/ocpi/<partner>/`; a new partner's captures exist before go-live
L1 refunds are now capped at €25 per session; anything larger goes to the `finance` queue in `backoffice` for a second approval
Tried an open-source OCPP simulator for load tests, but it lacked 2.0.1 and produced unrealistic meter curves; `cmd/cpsim` in the monorepo now simulates 10k chargers
Before each `cpgw` release, `cpsim` holds 10,000 connections on staging for 2 h at 3,000 msg/s, and p99 CALL latency must stay under 250 ms
Argo CD reverted a prod hotfix because someone had used `kubectl set image` directly; RBAC now blocks manual changes and only `vg-deploy` commits touch prod
Chargers with a space or `#` in their serial never connected because `cpgw` matched the raw path; ids are now percent-decoded and checked against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{3,48}$`
Charger search in `driverapi` uses PostGIS `ST_DWithin` on `evse_locations.geog` within 25 km, returns at most 200 EVSEs and leaves clustering to the apps
The portal map shows only the signed-in host's own sites with live connector status from `hostapi`; other hosts' chargers never appear, even nearby
`roamd` PATCHes EVSE status to partners through OCPI Locations within 30 s of a StatusNotification, debounced to one PATCH per connector per minute
TODO: publish tariffs through the OCPI tariffs module; partners still get prices by spreadsheet and show drivers estimates
Partners saw Ampfort EVSEs flip between AVAILABLE and CHARGING because they report `SuspendedEVSE` while throttled by `loadmgr`; that status now maps to CHARGING
TODO: Plug & Charge (ISO 15118-2) contract certificates for Kestrel DC150s once their 2.0.1 firmware ships; it needs a V2G root from a PKI vendor
OCPI START_SESSION from an eMSP goes `roamd` to `sessiond` to the owning `cpgw` pod; the CommandResult is POSTed to `response_url` once the charger answers or times out
Tried putting an MQTT broker ahead of the gateway to reuse its clustering, but OCPP needs request and reply on one WebSocket and CALL correlation broke; `cpgw` stays native WS
Host onboarding in `hostapi` creates the site in `assets.sites`, pre-registers each charger's `cpId` and credentials, and emails the installer a config sheet
Tried letting chargers self-register on their first BootNotification, but mistyped serials and squatters created phantom sites; pre-registration stays mandatory
UpdateFirmware is scheduled only between 02:00 and 05:00 in the site's zone and never while that unit has a running session
`vg-sql-billing` is a separate Postgres 16 instance for `billd` and `payoutd`, recoverable to any point in the last 35 days, against 7 days on `vg-sql-core`
Cloud SQL maintenance windows are Sunday 03:00 UTC for `vg-sql-core` and Wednesday 03:00 UTC for `vg-sql-billing`, so month-end invoicing never overlaps
40 Brightwatt units got stuck in a boot loop when their firmware URL expired mid-download; links are now signed GCS URLs valid 24 h and rollouts go 5% of a model at a time
TODO: store OCPP `SecurityEventNotification`s in `assets.security_events` and alert when one site reports repeated certificate failures
`vg_analytics.sessions_daily` is a scheduled query at 04:00 UTC over `vg_raw` that feeds both the host dashboard and finance's Looker Studio reports
Datastream replays after a Cloud SQL failover duplicated rows in the append-only `vg_raw.charge_sessions`; `sessions_daily` now keeps the latest `updated_at` per `id`
Portal revenue widgets call `hostapi` endpoints backed by BigQuery with a 15-minute cache; live connector status still comes from Postgres
The portal's uptime widget scanned all of `vg_raw.ocpp_frames` on every load, about €300 in one day; the table now has `require_partition_filter` set
When a charger replays queued transactions after an outage, `sessiond` accepts a StopTransaction for a session it never saw start and rebuilds it from meter values
Sessions were billed twice when a Kestrel charger replayed a queued StopTransaction after reconnecting; a repeat stop for a closed session is now a no-op
A session with no meter value or stop for 48 h is force-closed by `sessiond` with reason `stale`, priced on its last reading and flagged for support
Kept every meter sample in Postgres `meter_samples`, but it grew ~40 GB a month and autovacuum fell behind; Postgres now keeps start, end and hourly readings, BigQuery the rest
Tried GraphQL for `driverapi` so the apps could shape responses, but caching and per-field auth got messy and both app teams asked for REST back; it stays OpenAPI
Tried Firebase Remote Config for app feature flags, but flags then lived in two places; the apps read them from `driverapi` `/v1/config`, built from `flags.yaml`
Ran the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy as a sidecar, but it restarted apart from the app and broke readiness during rollouts; services now use the Cloud SQL Go connector with IAM auth
Tried a Bluetooth start path in the apps for underground car parks with no signal, but only one charger model had BLE; drivers there use the Voltgrid RFID card
QR scans from some camera apps failed because they percent-encoded the `*` in raw EVSE ids and the lookup compared encoded strings; stickers now carry the opaque `evseUid`
QR sticker URLs `go.voltgrid.eu/c/{evseUid}` open the app when installed, otherwise a page with the current price and store links that cannot start a session
TODO: ad hoc start from the QR web page for AC chargers without a terminal, once Kontant supports pre-authorization on its hosted payment page
Voltgrid RFID cards are MIFARE DESFire EV3 with 7-byte UIDs, issued from `backoffice` and linked to the driver in `id_tokens` with a `card_serial`
Some Voltgrid cards were refused because Ampfort readers send only the first 4 bytes of a 7-byte UID; `id_tokens` also indexes a `uid4` prefix for 8-hex-char idTags
Services export OpenTelemetry traces to Cloud Trace at 5% sampling, and at 100% for any `cpId` listed in `debug_chargers`
Go services log JSON with `log/slog` to stdout; keys are snake_case and every charger-related line carries `cp_id` and `evse_uid`
Only four alerts page: charger connections down >5% in 10 min, a non-empty DLQ, >50 CDR push failures an hour, and a failed invoice run; the rest open tickets
Stopping a session from the iOS lock-screen notification did nothing because the app was suspended before the call finished; the stop now runs in a background URLSession
Android showed €0,46/kWh for a €0.4589 tariff because the currency formatter defaulted to 2 decimals; per-kWh prices now render with up to 4
`payoutd` builds host statements from `invoice-issued-v1` events and contract terms fetched from `hostapi` over gRPC, storing them in its own `payouts` database
`loadmgr` reads each site's grid cap from `assets.sites.grid_cap_a` and live phase currents from `Current.Import` samples on `meter-values-v2`
Connector status changes go on `connector-status-v1`; `roamd`, `hostapi` and `driverapi` keep separate projections so one slow consumer never delays the others
`backofficed` has no database of its own; it calls the owning services' gRPC admin APIs, so support actions pass the same validation as everything else
`invoice-issued-v1` fans out to `notifyd`, which emails the receipt, and to `payoutd`, which books the host's share of each paid invoice
Secrets live in Secret Manager and reach pods as files through the CSI driver; env vars never hold secrets, and each service has its own GSA via Workload Identity
A restore of `vg-sql-billing` into `vg-staging` is rehearsed on the first Monday of each quarter; the last one took 38 minutes end to end
New OCPI partners start on `ocpi.staging.voltgrid.eu` with test tokens and must match 50 test sessions end to end before prod credentials are issued
Both apps ship every two weeks via staged rollout (Play 10%, 50%, 100%; App Store phased release); a crash rate above 0.5% halts it
Portal users are `owner`, `manager` or `viewer` per host; only owners see payout statements and bank details, and owners must use MFA
Go tests are written table-driven, `t.Run` names reading as sentences; no testify, just plain comparisons and `cmp.Diff` for structs
Numeric fields carry their unit in the name (`energy_wh`, `power_w`, `price_micros`, `timeout_s`); a bare `amount` or `energy` field fails review
Each architecture decision gets an ADR file under `docs/adr/` numbered `NNNN-title.md`; changing one means a new ADR that marks the old one superseded
Every Compose and SwiftUI screen has previews in light, dark and Dutch; PR screenshots come from those previews
Public APIs return errors in RFC 9457 problem+json form with a stable `type` URI under `api.voltgrid.eu/problems/`; apps branch on `type`, never on the text
